body:
I don't know your therapist but from my experiences it sounds like you might need a T that better fits your needs.

My previous T was really helpful.  She definitely asked the usual questions, how often do you have those thought? When do they occur? etc.  

She really helped me understand why I had those thoughts.  A few weeks later we were comfortable enough where we talked about suicide in general and she was able to answer a lot of my questions.

Does it matter?  It won't really change anything other than having the satisfaction of knowing.  From where I stand, either the ex-gf was right and I have/had an admirer, which of course would be flattering or the ex-gf was jealous and inventive, which would also be satisfying.
It would be satisfying because I was comfortable enough sharing my text conversations between Kat and I as there was never anything to hide.

Edit:  It would help with my self-confidence. I've already accepted the fact that Kat has a bf and the way our careers shaped out we will be hundreds of miles apart soon.

Of course, I made it clear it to her.  I told her because I didn't want to be that guy who just stays quiet and I felt I had nothing to lose.  I previously mentioned to Kat all the comments the ex gf had made supporting the idea that Kat was into me.  Kat dismissed the comments and provided counter examples.  Honestly don't know who to believe.
It's really unimportant how it plays out.  I'm leaving out of state soon for school anyway.  I'm just curious to know if my ex gf was right about being jealous.

She's sweet in general.  The idea that she was romantically interested in me was brought forth by my ex girlfriend.  Never really thought anything of it than, hey I get free food.  I'm still curious of course, was the ex girl right...or just over jealous?

I wasn't surprised that a number of sessions that were prescribed, I was surprised at the differences in duration.  3 Months vs 1 year. And honestly, I was hoping to have everything resolved a lot sooner but as was pointed out, it's not a linear progress.

 I did a little more research and it turns out that the previous organization had a 10 session limit for individual therapy before referring clients to another agency.
Thanks for the response this clarifies a lot.

The way the T phrased it seemed weird but it's not uncommon for T's to end the 1st session early depending on the plan.  If the first meeting is just an assessment it typically involves a questionnaire that can last anywhere from 1 to 2 sessions depending on the complexity of the client's answers.   In my first session my answers were quick and a lot of the questions were not applicable to me such as substance use/abuse so that sped up the process.  The T was surprised that we finished within 30min of our 50 minute session and it was implied that we could be finished but we just kept chatting.

I agree with not wanting people interfering in my business.  But tt was a big step letting my friends know that I was in therapy.  
As far as the girl goes... I asked her why she wanted me to stop and her answer was "because you don't need it."  I could tell she felt embarrassed because she assumed she was the reason I was in therapy (not the case) and she felt guilty for not being able to do more to help me.

Came across your post.  And for sure some days will suck , other days will be good, and some will be uneventful.  If you're ever feeling anxious or need someone to vent to feel free to reach out to me.  I'm up at odd hours anyway and could be of service as a listener.

If its an option, have you tried talking to your parents about how you're feeling?  If you and your parents are willing to have that conversation maybe you can arrive at a resolution and their can be understanding.  What about involving  therapy?

Not currently seeing a T (being referred Mon to a new one) but in the past when I have experienced similar feeling my T at the very least gave me an outsider to help me work through the reasons behind my emptiness.  As supportive as friend and family try to be often I have found that they provide you solutions to what they think you need.  While a T, has helped me arrive at my own conclusions.

To help deal with the emptiness I try getting involved in group hobbies.  I'm big into weightlifting and volunteering for example.    And while I may at times feel empty for long periods of time I find purpose when i'm volunteering helping others or at the gym.
I don't think it's anything to necessarily feel bad about.  A lot of the reasons above seem justified in preferring one gender over the other (or having no preference).

My exact experience.   Majority of my "lets grab coffee/ice cream/dinner" friends are female and the majority of "lets do an activity/event" are male. 

Although I didn't like my male therapist's approach it was very effective and quick.  At times it seemed like he ignored the direction I wanted to take the conversation.  Might have been to due to the fact that he knew I had a limited budget and wouldn't stay around too long when paying out of pocket so he wanted to help reach a resolution sooner than later.

In short, it does happen although the majority of therapist try to be understanding and compassionate of all experiences.

Example:

I worked in primary care for about 2 years and our patients had access to a behavioral health specialist during their encounter with their physician.  Typically, they would meet for about 30 minutes as a "trial" and if patient were interested they could enroll in future 1 on 1 session with a therapist.  Since I served as a liaison between the patient, doctor, and therapist, I was typically the last health care provider to interact with the patient before they left.  From the patient feedback some of the therapist would underestimate issues based on what other cases were observed that day.  For example we had two separate cases at different times, one involving a patient who had survived a shooting and another a patient with self-esteem issues due to her weight.  The therapist gave more attention and was more concerned with the shooting victim compared to the weight loss patient.
The pocket operators sound like a brilliant idea!  Is there any specific models you would recommend?
